questions.question_text: In the integral $\int\left(4x^{5} + 9\right)dx$, which part is the integrand?

options.why: The $dx$ names the variable of integration, not the function being integrated.
The integral sign shows the operation; the integrand is the function it acts on.
Includes the constant of integration, which belongs to the answer rather than to the integrand.

questions.solution_text:
The integrand is the function written between the integral sign and the $dx$.
Here that is $4x^{5} + 9$.

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly distinguishes $\int_{2}^{6} g(x)\,dx$ from $\int g(x)\,dx$?

options.text: $\int_{2}^{6} g(x)\,dx$ is a number, while $\int g(x)\,dx$ is a family of functions.
$\int_{2}^{6} g(x)\,dx$ is a function of $x$, while $\int g(x)\,dx$ is a number.
options.why: Reverses the two; adding limits turns an integral into a number, not into a function.

options.text: Both are numbers, but only the second one needs $+C$.
options.why: An integral with no limits has no numerical value at all; it is a family of functions.

options.text: Both are functions, and the limits only change the value of the constant.
options.why: Substituting the limits produces a value, not a function, and the constant cancels in the subtraction.

questions.solution_text:
Limits turn an integral into a single number.
$\int_{2}^{6} g(x)\,dx$ is a number, and $\int g(x)\,dx = G(x) + C$ is a family of functions.
